name: LADA 2106 N20 TURBO
role: The white Lada 2106 (owner decision 2026-11-22, #25 c7081083460 / #26 c7081085893): a lightly tuned BMW N20B20 single-turbo inline-four from the day the player gets it. NOT stock, NOT the rotary, NO second turbo, NOT gated by stars. Same chassis numbers as the red Lada (grip, steering, yaw: the approved handling); its own engine, power, sound and acceleration.
spec: N20B20 2.0 TURBO I4 • STAGE 1 • ~275 PS / 410 NM (EST.)

confirmed: Donor engine BMW N20B20 (328i): 1,997 cc inline-four, one twin-scroll turbocharger, direct injection; 245 PS (180 kW) at 5,000-6,500 rpm and 350 Nm at 1,250-4,800 rpm (angurten.de data sheet, auto-data.net).

Owner decisions: white Lada = N20B20, tuned lightly FROM THE START (c7081083460, c7081085893); mechanical MANUAL gearbox, the game shifts (c7080962400); no second turbo is implied; an engine swap for stars is a FUTURE idea, not built.
estimates: Tuned output 275 PS / 410 Nm = a conservative Stage 1: the stock turbo and internals, an ECU map, a cone intake with a heat shield, a free-flow downpipe / exhaust and an upgraded intercooler. Published Stage 1 claims for the N20 are +22 to +62 hp (BimmerWorld Stage 1+ +22 hp / +22 lb-ft with intercooler; Burger up to +35 hp / +50 lb-ft; Epic +44 hp / +68 lb-ft; Weistec W.1 +62 hp / +65 lb-ft: vendor figures, not dyno sheets). +30 PS / +60 Nm sits at the cautious end. The owner-suggested 280-290 PS / 400-420 Nm stays a PROVISIONAL proposal, not adopted.
Spark plugs and coils keep the ignition reliable at the higher boost; they are NOT counted as power.
Mass 1,150 kg = the red Lada's estimate (same shell, cage and a manual box; the N20 and the 13B are of similar weight), +-100 kg.
Gearing = the 5-speed table of the engine block (sound design): [44,76,110,148,190] km/h at 6,500 rpm, so the top gear reaches about 200 km/h at the limiter. The real box and final drive are MISSING.
missing: Real gearbox + final drive (a manual 6-speed from the donor or a Lada box?), tyre size, build mass, the exact tune, dyno / GPS figures.

performance.reference: The v0.1.36 power-to-weight law anchored on the red Lada (see docs/CAR_PROFILES.md): 0-100 km/h = 3.29 s x 201 / 239 = 2.76 s in ARCADE_PLUS; REAL_POWER_TEST gives its own numbers.

handling_notes.source: Chassis numbers of the red Lada (the approved handling, bit-identical). Only drive_accel and drag_coeff differ: the power-to-weight calibration for 275 PS / 1,150 kg = 239 PS/t (0-100 km/h 2.76 s, solved with the same procedure as the E30 and the RYU-32 in v0.1.36).

engine_notes.physical_layout: Inline-four, firing order 1-3-4-2, the twin-scroll turbine takes cylinders 1+4 and 2+3: two exhaust banks of two (bank [0,1,0,1] in firing order).
engine_notes.character: Dull, turbine-muffled exhaust with a bark from the free-flow downpipe, a thin airbox intake, a rising compressor whistle with boost, a short flutter when the throttle closes, a little DIY roughness (jitter 0.02), overrun burble from the tune (misfire 0.24). 6,900 rpm limiter, idle 820.
engine_notes.not_car_data: Gear ratios, the final drive and the exact limiter of the real build are unknown; the numbers are sound design in the character of a tuned N20.

arcade_plus.basis: = the REAL_POWER_TEST top speed rounded down to 5 km/h: the ESTIMATED 5-speed table at the 6,900 rpm limiter (201.7 km/h); the power / drag limit of 275 PS is about 245 km/h, so the (unknown) gearing sets the top.

confirmed: Stock N20B20: 245 PS at 5,000-6,500 rpm, 350 Nm at 1,250-4,800 rpm (the plateau of the table is the stock shape lifted by the tune).
estimates: Tuned curve: 410 Nm plateau from 1,600 to 4,500 rpm, about 274 PS flat from 5,000 to 5,750 rpm, falling to 255 Nm at the 6,900 rpm limiter. Shape = the stock plateau scaled by the Stage 1 gain; the numbers between the points are interpolation.
Mass 1,150 kg, Cd*A 0.85 m2 (the Lada body), efficiency 0.85, rolling 0.012, launch 5.5 m/s2, gear table as in the engine block.
missing: Real gearbox + final drive, tyres, mass, the exact tune, boost / lag behaviour (turbo lag is NOT modelled: the table is a steady-state curve).
